transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Carva Coleman.
This year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine goes to three scientists, Karl Deisterot,
Peter Hegeman and Georg Nagel.
They've researched ways to study the brain.
The Nobel Committee says they've looked at ways to switch on or off the activity of individual
nerve cells in a living brain.
The investigation into last week's attack and a passenger jet headed to Tel Aviv finds
the co-pilot intended to crash the jet into Israel's Ben Gurion Airport.
That's according to a person familiar with the matter but not authorized to speak publicly.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf says there's no clear motive for the attack.
This morning, a source familiar with the investigation told NPR that the co-pilot who attacked the
captain intended to fly the plane to Ben Gurion Airport, which was its destination, but then
crash it into the airport.
This all happened in the morning here when Ben Gurion would have been full of people.
That source also said that it's likely the co-pilot acted alone.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reporting.
President Trump has named a new czar who will oversee artificial intelligence policy.
He will also help lead a new White House team that will be focused on AI technology.
NPR's Chantalice Duster has more.
President Trump says Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton is the new White House
AI czar and will help lead his superintelligence force.
After Trump's meeting with AI leaders last week, Clayton pushed back on calls to pause
developing the technology during an interview with CNBC.
To somehow say we should back away from this and let the rest of the world develop these
models and implement these models.
I don't think anybody in that room and I don't think any American should think that that's
a good strategy.
It is unclear what Clayton's appointment as AI czar means for the AI industry as current
artificial intelligence regulation by the U.S. government is limited.
Chantalice Duster, NPR News.
In Los Angeles, a woman of Chinese descent has been arrested.
She is accused of spying on the family of a high-ranking Taiwanese official, reportedly
the president.
Steve Futterman reports.
The arrest took place at Los Angeles International Airport.
Law enforcement officials say the 34-year-old woman, Wanying Zhang, was about to board a
plane to China.
She is accused of spying on the family of a senior Taiwan official on behalf of the
Chinese government and is charged with acting as an unregistered foreign agent.
The Justice Department says Zhang, at the direction of China, supplied pictures, videos,
and license plate information of the Taiwan leader's family.
She is due to make her first court appearance on Monday, a statement from the office of
Taiwan's president thanked the U.S. government for what it called protecting Taiwanese citizens.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles.
This is NPR.
President Trump is going to campaign in Nebraska today with Republican Senator Pete Ricketts.
The incumbent GOP senator is facing a strong challenge from independent candidate Dan Osborne.
He is supported by national Democrats.
Trump has been facing criticism from U.S. ranchers, including those in Nebraska, to
allow beef imports.
At least one person is dead and half a dozen more injured following Russian airstrikes
on several of Ukraine's main cities.
The attacks came as Russia's defense ministry said it was dramatically increasing its attacks.
NPR's Charles Maines reports from Moscow that as even as the war crossed the four-and-a-half
year mark.
Russia said it targeted industrial and port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odessa region,
as well as a power station in Kharkiv in the east.
That followed weekend airstrikes on key bridges in Kiev that have snarled movement in Ukraine's
capital.
Russia's defense ministry has vowed to intensify strikes in what it says is Ukrainian military
infrastructure, a direct response to ministry claim to Ukraine's months-long campaign of
targeting Russian energy facilities.
That Russia's attacks, primarily using jet-powered drones and ballistic missiles, also seemed
time to take full advantage of Ukraine's dwindling air defenses, destroying critical
heating and energy systems ahead of the winter months.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
Brazil's presidential election will go to a runoff vote.
Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil's former right-wing president, leads left-wing incumbent
Luis Anacio Lula da Silva in yesterday's voting.
The next election is October 25th.
It's NPR.
